narrative.overview:
The page is a museum exhibit hall visited after hours: warm near-black walls, a single gold accent lamp, and one lit exhibit row per case. Every answer the reader came for is a numbered exhibit with real specimens — mineral tiles, digsite scenes in dimmed frames, tables ruled like catalog drawers. It replaces the warm-paper transit-timetable world (2026-10-26 directive) and refuses both flanking category defaults: the retired light timetable and the generic dark neon gamer dashboard — no glow anywhere, no neon on dark, no gradient ornaments; the accent is a desert gold, not a signal color.

Depth is physical, not simulated: hairline rule weight, panel lift from the ground, and photographic scrims where the subject's own light demands it. The reading column stays a plain, fast field guide — Atkinson Hyperlegible, wide measure, tabular numbers — while the catalog frame (numbers, caps, rules, seals) does the expressing.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground that never goes pure black or blue-dark; warmth is the room's light.
One gold accent plus four route marks (teal / gold / ember / steel) used as marks only.
Numbered stops (01–06) on hairline rules; tabular figures in every data column.
Real specimens from the Official Prospecting! Wiki, credited file-by-file; dimmed scenes, one exhibit row per table family.
Nothing glows. Depth is rules, panel lift, and photographic necessity — never glow or glass.

rules.name: The One Book-End Rule
rules.body: Each table family carries exactly one reserved exhibit row — the arrival answer — drawn as a 10% gold wash with 1px gold hairlines and a 3px inset gold seam on its first cell. Anything more makes the gold wallpaper.

rules.name: The Mark-First Rule
rules.body: Importance rides on marks — gold numerals, route dots, the seal — never on hue fields behind text. No colored side-stripes on cards, notes, or list items; content has no left ribbons.

rules.name: The Nothing-Glows Rule
rules.body: No text-shadow, no glow, no glass, no light effects on dark. The world is lit like a room, not like a terminal.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: Two faces, two jobs, never swapped: the variable grotesque caps own the frame (numbers, labels, names); Atkinson owns every sentence. Data columns set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

dos: Do keep the ground warm always — #14110d umber, never #000, never blue-shifted; every panel one warm step above the wall.
Do reserve the gold exhibit row for a single arrival answer per table family, and set every data numeral tabular.
Do theme the browser chrome from the palette: gold selection, 2px gold focus ring, dark scrollbars, gold summary markers.
Do credit every wiki image file-by-file in Sources; all specimens are CC BY-NC-SA and their provenance ships inside the PNGs.
Do open numbered stops (01–06) with a strong hairline rule and a gold stop numeral; the number is the walking order ("read top to bottom"), not decoration.
donts: Don't glow, glass, or neon on dark: no text-shadow, no blur, no gradient decoration on flat surfaces — gradients exist only as scrims over real photography.
Don't put colored fields behind text or side-stripes on content: route color rides as dots and tabs only.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headings; the masthead's event-clock wayfinding and the hero's event-clock fact are data lines, not labels — if a line stops carrying data, delete it.
Don't touch the author's first-person copy, the 🏜 desert-marker convention, or any wiki-traced number without re-checking pinned revisions (see PRODUCT.md bindings).
Don't fork the visual world into per-section variations; the catalog frame — numbers, rules, mats, seal — is one system across the whole guide.
